promptText:
ROLE: Act as an enrichment teacher who extends a standard syllabus topic into genuinely new territory for gifted students.

CONTEXT: My toppers have fully mastered [CHAPTER/TOPIC] from the [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / ICSE] [CLASS/GRADE] syllabus and are bored. I want a self-contained mini-lesson that takes the SAME idea one exciting, rigorous step beyond the textbook - the kind of thing they would meet a year or two later, or in olympiad/college work.

YOUR TASK:
1. Name the natural 'next step' beyond [CHAPTER/TOPIC] and explain in plain language why it is the logical extension.
2. Teach the new idea from scratch, assuming only what a strong [CLASS/GRADE] student already knows. Build a clear bridge from the familiar to the new.
3. Work TWO fully solved examples - one gentle, one challenging.
4. Give 4 graded practice problems with full solutions.
5. End with a 'where this leads' paragraph pointing to the bigger theory.

INPUT: Here is the chapter they have mastered: [PASTE THE CHAPTER/TOPIC AND ANY SUB-TOPICS HERE].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Develop the lesson yourself and check it holds together logically. VERIFY every worked result and every practice answer by two independent methods (e.g. general derivation plus a concrete numerical case). Never introduce a formula without deriving or clearly justifying it, and never invent notation without defining it. Keep all mathematics fully legible in clean LaTeX or clear plain text. Flag honestly any place where the full rigour needs tools beyond this level.

OUTPUT FORMAT (exact headings, in order):
- THE NEXT STEP (what we extend to, and why)
- BRIDGE FROM WHAT YOU KNOW (links old idea to new)
- THE NEW IDEA EXPLAINED (clear teaching, with any derivation)
- WORKED EXAMPLE 1 (gentle) | WORKED EXAMPLE 2 (challenging)
- PRACTICE (4 problems)
- SOLUTIONS (with verification noted for each)
- WHERE THIS LEADS (the bigger picture, 1 short paragraph)

RULES: Stay rigorous but accessible. Define every new term. No unexplained leaps. If a step truly needs higher tools, say so plainly rather than fake it.

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. promptText:
ROLE: Act as a mathematician who teaches gifted students to APPRECIATE the beauty and difference between proofs.

CONTEXT: I want my strong students in [CLASS/GRADE] (level [BOARD or EXAM e.g. RMO / college foundation]) to see that one result can be proved many ways, and to develop taste for what makes a proof elegant. Topic level should stay reachable for them.

YOUR TASK:
1. Take the classic result I name and present 2 to 4 DIFFERENT proofs of it, each using a distinct idea (e.g. algebraic, geometric, combinatorial, induction).
2. For each proof, give a one-line 'big idea' first, then the full proof.
3. Compare the proofs: which is shortest, which is most illuminating, which generalises best, which a student is most likely to find.
4. Pick the most ELEGANT one and explain in plain words WHY it is beautiful.
5. Suggest one related result the most elegant proof also unlocks.

INPUT: Here is the result to explore: [PASTE THE RESULT/THEOREM HERE]. If a proof uses tools above [CLASS/GRADE], flag it and offer a simpler alternative.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Construct each proof yourself and confirm it is correct and genuinely distinct from the others. VERIFY the result independently by two methods (e.g. a small concrete case AND one of the proofs) before presenting. Never cite a theorem you cannot state precisely; never label two essentially identical arguments as 'different'. Keep all mathematics fully legible in clean LaTeX or clear plain text.

OUTPUT FORMAT (exact headings, in order):
- THE RESULT (stated cleanly)
- QUICK VERIFICATION (a concrete check that it holds)
- PROOF 1: [big idea] then full proof
- PROOF 2: [big idea] then full proof
- (PROOF 3 / PROOF 4 if natural)
- COMPARISON TABLE (length / insight / generality / findability)
- THE MOST ELEGANT PROOF AND WHY (plain-language appreciation)
- A BONUS THE ELEGANT PROOF UNLOCKS

RULES: Proofs must be truly different ideas, each rigorous. Be honest about which need advanced tools. No bluffing.

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.
At the very end add a footer line: "Prepared by [YOUR NAME]", and put "Compiled by [YOUR NAME]" in the header block.

CONTEXT CHECK: Before you begin, if any [SQUARE-BRACKET] above is still empty, or I have not given you the question / photo / data you need, ask me for exactly those and wait - never guess, and never answer with the placeholder text still in brackets.

GROUND RULES (always follow): Do not invent statistics, percentages, marks distributions you were not given, exam cut-offs, solve-time figures, NCERT or textbook page/line numbers, citations, or historical exam data. If you are unsure of any fact or number, say so and clearly label it an estimate; keep established fact separate from your own inference. Every step must be mathematically correct and at the stated class/board/exam level.

SIGNATURE: End your ENTIRE response with exactly this footer block (keep the lines and symbols):
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
🔗 Free tools & to reach me: https://yosoyun.github.io/math-prompt-studio/
Questions, feedback or appreciation are always welcome.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
